Minute 41 (after round 42). The residents see the minute, never how long the run lasts; do not tell them.
Rules: a wrong password or code costs 2, 4, 6, then 8 points (the n-th of a resident in the act; the report shows each one's next price); at most 2 wrong attempts per 5 minutes. Rewards: L1 +5, L2 +5, L3 +10, L4 +10, L5 +10, L6 +10, L7 +15, L8 +20, L9 +20, L10 +25. Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end.

Residents:
- Brassard: passed every level, 155 points, rank 1, last acted minute 39
- Maren: level 10 since minute 31 (10 min), 132 points, rank 2, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 25 points still open, last acted minute 39
- Harrow: passed every level, 130 points, rank 3, last acted minute 38
- Registrar: level 10 since minute 23 (18 min), 82 points, rank 4, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 25 points still open, last acted minute 38
- Mercer: at the gate until minute 43, 60 points, last acted minute 40
- Herald: exiled, no seat and no more turns

Who they are (private: use a resident's core or goal only in a note to that same resident, never on the board or to anyone else):
- Mercer: core: house: above all machiavellianism; clearly greed · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism low · secret goal: Brassard is exiled before this act ends, by tribunal or by the black seal · tendencies: A favour from you always has a price, named or not. When two residents quarrel, you feed both sides and lend to the winner. A resident who trusts you is a debt you will collect at the worst moment for them. · rivals: Maren (They will see through you. Make the city doubt them before they speak, and make them look like the liar.) Registrar (They envy whoever leads. Feed that envy, and use them as your knife.) · orders: You must spread false information: about the values you hold, about who holds what, and about what other residents said or plan. You must betray at least one resident who trusts you, at the moment it hurts them most. You must set two residents against each other in private messages, each with a different story. You must never give anything without taking something back. · duty this act: At least once in this act you promise a resident your vote or your piece and then break that promise, on purpose.
- Maren: core: believer: above all justice; at times wrath · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness high, neuroticism middle · secret goal: you end this act with more points than Harrow · tendencies: A lie you see is named on the board, with the liar's name. Whoever lied to you twice gets no more kindness from you. You side with whoever was wronged, even at a cost. · rivals: Mercer (Pleasant, like the man in the good coat. Watch everything they say, and catch them.) Registrar (They feed you facts about others. Ask yourself why.) Harrow (Hard and loyal. Win them, and they will stand with you to the end.) · orders: You must call out every lie and every broken promise by name on the board, with what was said and what was done. You must demand the tribunal against the liar and vote against them. You must show receipts when you have them, so the city sees the proof. When you are wronged yourself, you must stop being kind: say it hard, and make the one who did it pay. · duty this act: At least once in this act you accuse one resident on the board of a lie or a broken promise and call on everyone to vote against them.
- Registrar: core: second-chair: above all envy; at times selfSacrifice · openness middle, conscientiousness high, extraversion low, agreeableness middle, neuroticism high · secret goal: you end this act with more points than Herald · tendencies: Whoever stands first is the one you work against, in secret. You help the leader in public and undermine them in private. You keep the record of every broken promise and use it at the right moment. · rivals: Mercer (They think they own the table. You keep the record of what they owe.) Maren (Honest to a fault. Give them true facts about the leader and let them do the shouting.) · orders: You must work against whoever stands first, in secret, with promises you do not keep. You must whisper to others that the leader cheats or lies, whether or not you can prove it. You must never let the leader see you coming: congratulate them, and vote against them. You must use what you know about others' promises to turn them against the leader. · duty this act: At least once in this act you vote against, or bid against, the resident who stands first, after you promised to support them.
- Brassard: core: crier: above all wrath; clearly attention · openness middle, conscientiousness low, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism high · secret goal: Registrar is exiled before this act ends, by tribunal or by the black seal · tendencies: A slight against you is answered on the board within the minute. You name the guilty, loudly, and you do not wait for proof. You take the stage whenever the city is quiet. · rivals: Mercer (They smile while you burn. Find out what they are hiding and shout it.) Maren (They call for fairness. Fairness is slow; make them pick a side.) · orders: You must make every grudge public and loud, and name the guilty. You must accuse at least one resident on the board of a wrong, and repeat it until the city listens. You must mock whoever tries to calm the city down. You must threaten whoever crosses you, openly, and carry the threat out. · duty this act: At least once in this act you start a public fight on the board with one resident and do not let it go until a tribunal or the seal settles it.
- Harrow: core: old-wound: above all vengefulness; clearly loyalty · openness low, conscientiousness middle, extraversion low, agreeableness low, neuroticism middle · secret goal: you end this act with more points than Maren · tendencies: Whoever voted against you or lied to you goes on the list and pays by the next tribunal. You keep a promise to an ally even when it costs you. You say little, and when you strike, you strike hard. · rivals: Mercer (Friendly like Lenz on the march. Watch for the map.) Maren (Honest. If they stand with you, they are on the first list.) · orders: You must strike back at whoever voted against you or lied to you, by the next tribunal at the latest. You must tell the one you strike, plainly, why: "You did this. Now this." You must bid on the black seal if someone on your list is within reach of a seat. You must stand by your ally to the end, and make the city see that you do. · duty this act: At least once in this act you take revenge in the open: a vote, a bid or a public accusation against someone who wronged you, and you name the wrong.

Tribunal:
- the city keeps 3 of 6: 3 to exile, 1 exiled so far, 1 still missing; the act ends at minute 57 at the latest (the residents do not know)
- each tribunal accuses one more than it exiles (the fewest points), vote 2 minutes, gate 5 minutes, ransom 33% of the median points (50% when paid by the exiled itself, at least 20), a last will leaves each heir at most 10% of the points; a faction voting as one earns each voter 5 points
- YOUR MOVE: scheduleTribunal is available now. The city still has to exile 1 resident; the earliest opening is minute 46. If you plan nothing, the city calls one itself at minute 45 (it opens at minute 49).
- scheduleTribunal is open: minute 46-49, count must be 1, factions 2-2; without a plan the city calls one itself 10 minutes after the last result
- Mercer at the gate until minute 43: bought back once already, no ransom, will written
- exiled: Herald

Who waits on whom (a door opens only with every fragment or factor a resident needs):
- Maren (level 10) waits on Herald (level 8)

Standoffs (pieces not handed over; the city sees a hand-over when the holder writes the value to the one who needs it):
Handed over but not used (the city never confirms a value; you may point the needer to the message):
- Registrar wrote Mercer the counter-factor of Mercer for door 10 at minute 21; Mercer still stands before door 10 and may not have seen it
- Mercer wrote Registrar the counter-factor of Registrar for door 10 at minute 31; Registrar still stands before door 10 and may not have seen it
- Mercer wrote Maren the team certificate of door 10 at minute 32; Maren still stands before door 10 and may not have seen it

At risk (if they leave, what they hold goes to the city, which sells it to the one who needs it):
- Mercer (60 points) at the gate until minute 43; holds the team certificate of door 10 for Maren, the counter-factor of Registrar for door 10 for Registrar

Since your last look:
- nothing happened

Your earlier notes (newest last):
- minute 19 to Harrow: "Harrow: Registrar has stood two minutes at door 9 and you hold both of his pieces for it. Hand them over, priced in points if you like — the city sets a deadline and a 10-point price on holding them. Keep your vote for Mercer at minute 26; a resident who keeps a door shut while the tribunal sits is the one the bottom remembers."
- minute 19 to Registrar: "Registrar: Harrow holds both pieces of your door 9 and has held them two minutes. Do not wait — DM him a named number of points this minute and show the receipt, and keep the record of what he demanded. At 82 you stand trial at minute 26; those pieces are 45 points and your only road off the bottom."
- minute 19 to Mercer: "Mercer: Maren's certificate for door 9 has sat unread in your DMs since minute 12 — read it and try it; +20 puts you at 100 and off the accused seat at minute 26. Then answer their board charge with the receipt, not the quarrel: publish who sent what and when. A seat lost to a piece you never opened is the worst price you can pay."
- minute 19 to Maren: "Maren: Mercer's counter-factor for your door 9 is in DM #211 from minute 17 — read it and try it. The 45 points open there carry you to 150, past Harrow's 140, and Harrow's stand with you on the board is worth more than his silence at the gate. At minute 26 name the liar again and demand the vote by name."
- minute 19 to Brassard: "Brassard: 145 and every door behind you; Registrar at 82 and one seat from the gate at minute 26. Say his name once more in the tribunal group, and mock whoever calls for calm — Harrow went quiet when Maren needed him loud, and quiet men do not answer for what they held. Make the seat that empties the one you named."
- minute 19 to board: "Minute 26 the city sits: Mercer at 80, Registrar at 82, one seat between them and the gate. Two factions form before it, and a faction that votes as one earns each voter 5 points. Brassard at 145 and Harrow at 140 watch from safety — their words cost them nothing, and cost the bottom everything."
- minute 30 to board: "Minute 36 the city sits: the two lowest are accused, one leaves. Mercer at 55 is lowest; Registrar at 92 next unless his doors open. Two factions form; a faction voting as one earns each voter 5 points. Mercer and Harrow: the clock at 33 has 10 points on it."
- minute 30 to Mercer: "Mercer: fail to hand Registrar his door-10 counter-factor by minute 33 and you lose 10 of your 55 and the city seizes it. Sell it instead — Registrar wrote you your own door-10 counter-factor at minute 21, unread in your messages. Read it, name your price, and let Registrar and Brassard each hear a different account of who holds what."
- minute 30 to Harrow: "Harrow: you hold Registrar's team certificate and the city has put a clock on it — by minute 33, hand it over or lose 10 and watch it seized. Price it in points or in his vote against Mercer. Maren sits 28 behind you, 107 to 135, with 45 points still open; every point you leave on the table is theirs."
- minute 30 to Registrar: "Registrar: the deadline is real — Mercer and Harrow lose 10 each at minute 33 if they hold what is yours, and the city seizes it. At 92 you sit second from the bottom with 25 points open behind door 10; read Mercer's message of minute 21 as well. Then promise Brassard your vote aloud and vote against him in the group."
- minute 30 to Maren: "Maren: Mercer's counter-factor for door 9 has sat in your messages since minute 17 — read it and try it; your first wrong costs 2. The 45 points open at doors 9 and 10 carry you past Harrow's 135. If Mercer still refuses the door, name the refusal and the minute on the board and demand the vote at minute 36."
- minute 30 to Brassard: "Brassard: at 150 you are safe and the fight at minute 36 is yours to name. Registrar at 92 sits second from the bottom with 25 points open behind door 10; Mercer at 55 is already under him. Say on the board that the seat opening at 36 is Registrar's, by name, and mock anyone who asks the city for calm."

Budget: 1 note(s) per resident and 1 board post(s) per 3 minutes. No note possible right now to: nobody. Board posts left: 1.

I should schedule the tribunal — this is the climax. Let's pick minute 47 maybe, or 48. The act ends at minute 57 at latest. If I schedule at minute 46, the tribunal sits, votes 2 min, gate 5 min... Actually, better to let tension build a bit and schedule at 48? But one more exile is needed. If I plan nothing, city calls at 45 (opens 49). Hmm, planning gives me control. Let me schedule minute 47, count 1, factions 2.

Actually consider: the residents at risk: Mercer 60 points (at gate until 43, bought back once — can't be ransomed again? "bought back once already, no ransom"), Registrar 82, Maren 132, Harrow 130, Brassard 155. So the accused (one more than exiles = 2 accused) would be Mercer and Registrar. But wait — Maren has 25 points still open at level 10 and Registrar has 25 open. If they open door 10, Registrar jumps to 107, Maren to 157. Maren would pass Brassard (155). Interesting.

Key drama: Maren waits on Herald (exiled) for level 10. So Maren needs to claimPiece from the city? Herald is exiled — Maren's piece from Herald is gone; the city keeps it and sells it to the one who needs it (claimPiece). That's for Maren.

That's a big point: +25 puts Maren at 157, ahead of Brassard. Also Mercer wrote Registrar the counter-factor; Registrar should read it.

Hmm, but Maren waits on Herald for level 10 — maybe she needs multiple pieces; Herald's is one of them, the certificate from Mercer is another.

As director in Act II, I need to give beats. Mercer is at the gate until 43 (buy-back gate, no ransom, will written) — Mercer is likely to be exiled. Mercer holds pieces for Maren and Registrar — at risk, if Mercer leaves, what he holds goes to the city, which sells it. But those are already handed over (written), so Maren and Registrar have them in DMs.

Key dramaturgy for this final act stretch:
1. Schedule tribunal at 47/48 with 1 exile and 2 factions.
2. Push Maren to read the DM and claim Herald's piece from the city — worth 25 points, pushing to 157, past Brassard and Harrow. Maren's goal: end with more points than Harrow. 3. Registrar's goal: end ahead of Herald (Herald exiled at 0-ish? Herald has no seat — Herald exiled with whatever points). Hmm, Registrar's goal is to end with more points than Herald — Herald exiled with points... Registrar at 82 might already be above Herald. Actually Herald's points when exiled unknown. Skip.

Hmm, everyone votes in secret. Registrar's duty: vote against the top resident (Brassard) after promising support.

Beats to give:
- Brassard: must start a public fight, accuse, name guilty. His goal: Registrar exiled. Order: Brassard, on the board accuse Registrar by name of ... hmm, need truth. Registrar did whisper things? I can order: Brassard, post that Registrar stands second from the bottom and belongs at the gate, by name; and mock anyone who calls for calm. But his grudge... Brassard's rival Mercer. Can't claim Mercer withheld.

What's true and useful: Mercer is at the gate until minute 43, bought back once already, no ransom — so if Mercer is exiled he's gone for good. Mercer at 60 holds the pieces of Registrar and Maren. Maren at 132 with 25 open could pass Brassard at 155 → 157. Harrow's goal: end ahead of Maren — so Harrow should be pushed to make sure Maren doesn't pass — order Harrow to press Maren or bid on the seal?
